text:
lina: FYI I hit a reproducible hang in the go generator sample when cancelling during the auth refresh window. repro steps + tiny harness in the gist: https://internal.gists/redwood/stream-repro
marc: can you summarize the hang? stack trace?
oliver: usually these are `readLoop` or `authRefresh` goroutines waiting on channels after ctx canceled.
lina: exact: user calls `Subscribe` -> handshake starts -> token refresher kicks -> user ctx cancelled -> client returns but two goroutines remain: auth refresher and reader. they block on `authCh` send/recv. stack shows `github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/stream.(*reader).run` and `github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/auth.(*refresher).loop`.
jen: is this the case where the refresh loop writes to a channel without select on ctx.Done()? that would explain it.
lina: yes. simple fix in the refresher: select on ctx.Done() when trying to notify the stream. patch: ```go
select {
case authCh <- token:
case <-ctx.Done():
  return ctx.Err()
}
```
marc: good catch. but we should think API ergonomics: current public `Subscribe` returns a channel and runtime-managed goroutines which makes cancellation ownership ambiguous. new pattern: `Stream := client.Pull(ctx, req)` with `func (s *Stream) Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error)` + `Close()`. that makes cancellation explicit and forces callers to pass ctx into Recv.
oliver: that also aligns with typical Go io.Reader style and maps well to deadlines. we could implement a small adapter for backwards compat: `Subscribe` creates the stream and launches goroutine that calls `Recv` and pushes to user channel, but with proper ctx wiring so Close cancels both.
jen: tests please. add `TestStreamCancelDuringHandshake` that asserts no goroutine leaks (use go test -race + pprof goroutine count). I can add a harness in `sdk/go/examples/generator-cancel` and a unit test in `stream/stream_test.go`.
lina: I added that test to my branch, it fails on master with ~4 goroutines leaked per cancel, passes after patch. link: https://ci.internal/blue/streams/3741
marc: parity note: python and ts older clients handle this by closing net.Conn on cancel which unwinds other goroutines. Go should prefer explicit api (Recv(ctx)) but document differences. add a doc blurb in `docs/sdk/go/streaming.md` comparing behaviors.
oliver: UX: show example snippet for newbies showing `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(...)` and `defer cancel()` plus `defer stream.Close()`. folks copy paste those. also add a small linter warning in the example `// don't forget Close()`.
jen: performance: Recv(ctx) adds a tiny per-call ctx check but negligible vs network. add a benchmark in `stream/bench_test.go` to be safe.
dev-bot: created issue #5128 for "go: generator stream cancellation during auth refresh hangs" and linked PR candidate branch lina/stream-cancel.
lina: i'll open RFC proposing v2 streaming API w/ Recv(ctx)+Close, include migration shim and sample app update. tagging @marc @oliver @jen for review. thanks :raised_hands:
marc: if we go v2, make sure Dedicated customers get a migration note and compat layer in the client to avoid breakage for infra-heavy users.
jen: also update go sdk changelog and add a short snippet in the Console docs about generator backpressure and cancellation semantics.
oliver: cool. once RFC is up I'll run the perf matrix and help with python/ts parity notes.
